h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר נ׳ Pesach — Maamar Nun

p: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
In the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ס"א:):
מְזוֹנָא יַתִּיר דְּקִיק קָאתְיָא מֵאֲתַר דְּדִינָא אִשְׁתְּכַח, וְדָא הוּא מְזוֹנָא יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּד נְפָקוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם וְכוּלֵּי;
"A much finer sustenance comes from the place where Judgment is found, and that is the sustenance of Israel when they went out of Egypt [matzah], etc.";
וְאַחַר כָּךְ
and afterward
(ibid. 62a):

וְדָא הוּא בְּרִירוּ דְּמִלָּה: מְזוֹנָא קַדְמָאָה וְכוּלֵּי וְדָא מְזוֹנָא דְּגוּפָא; מְזוֹנָא עִילָּאָה מִינֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵּי מֵאֲתַר דְּדִינָא שַׁרְיָא, וְדָא הוּא מְזוֹנָא דְּמִסְכְּנָא וְכוּלֵּי; מְזוֹנָא עִילָּאָה יַתִּיר מֵאִילֵּין וְכוּלֵּי וְהוּא מְזוֹנָא דִּבְנֵי מַרְעֵי, הֲדָא הוּא דִּכְתִיב

"And this is the clarification of the matter: the first sustenance, etc., is the sustenance of the body [ordinary bread]; a sustenance higher than it, etc., comes from the place where Judgment rests, and that is the sustenance of the poor [matzah], etc.; a sustenance higher still than these, etc., is the sustenance of the sick [manna], as it is written
(תְּהִלִּים מ"א, ד'):
(Tehillim 41:4):
ה' יִסְעָדֶנּוּ עַל עֶרֶשׂ דְּוָי וְגוֹמֵר."
'Hashem will sustain him upon the sickbed, etc.'"
הִנֵּה מַה שֶּׁמְּדַמֶּה בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ מְזוֹן הַחוֹלֶה לַאֲכִילַת מָן—כִּי גַּם הַחוֹלֶה נִיזּוֹן בְּמָזוֹן נַפְשִׁי מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ה' יִסְעָדֶנּוּ עַל עֶרֶשׂ דְּוָי;

Now the holy Zohar's comparison of a sick person's nourishment to eating manna is understandable, because a sick person too is sustained with spiritual nourishment directly from heaven, as it is said "Hashem will sustain him upon the sickbed";

אֲבָל מַה שֶּׁמְּדַמֶּה מַאֲכַל אֶבְיוֹנִים לַאֲכִילַת מַצָּה—הֲלוֹא עַל אֲכִילַת מַצָּה מְבָרְכִין "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ", וְגַם כָּל הַשִּׁבְעָה יָמִים שֶׁהוּא רְשׁוּת כְּבָר אָמַרְנוּ

however, regarding its comparison of the food of the impoverished to eating matzah—surely over eating matzah we recite the blessing "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us," and even on all seven days when it is "optional," we have already explained
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ט"ז)
(as elucidated in Maamar 16)
שֶׁהוּא מִצְוָה, רַק מִצְוָה לְגַבֵּי חוֹבָה רְשׁוּת קָרֵי לֵיהּ—וּמַה זֶּה דִּמְיוֹן לַאֲכִילַת אֶבְיוֹנִים?!
that it is a positive mitzvah (only relative to a strict obligation is an optional mitzvah termed reshus)—so what is the comparison to the food of the destitute?!
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
One can explain this along the lines of what they said
(בְּרָכוֹת כ':):
(Berachos 20b):
כְּתִיב
It is written
(דְּבָרִים י', י"ז):
(Devarim 10:17):
אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשָּׂא פָנִים וְגוֹמֵר,
"Who shows no favoritism, etc.,"
וּכְתִיב
and it is written
(בְּמִדְבַּר ו', כ"ו):
(Bamidbar 6:26):
יִשָּׂא ה' פָּנָיו אֵלֶיךָ
"May Hashem lift His countenance [show favor] to you"
אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: וְכִי לֹא אֶשָּׂא פָּנִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם מְדַקְדְּקִים עַל עַצְמָם עַד כְּזַיִת וְעַד כְּבֵיצָה וְכוּלֵּי?!
"The Holy One, blessed is He, said: 'Shall I not show favor to Israel, who are scrupulous with themselves [to recite Grace After Meals] even over an olive's bulk or an egg's bulk, etc.'?!"
וּבְאַגָּדוֹת מַהַרְשָׁ"א שֶׁהוּא מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם נוֹשְׂאִים פָּנִים לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּמְדַקְדְּקִים בַּמִּצְוֹת.
And in Aggados Maharsha he explains that this is measure for measure, because they show deference to the Holy One, blessed is He, by being scrupulous in commandments.
וַעֲדַיִין קָשֶׁה לָמָּה תָּפְסוּ דַּוְקָא בָּזֶה יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁאָר דִּקְדּוּקֵי מִצְוֹת?
Yet it is still difficult: why did the Sages single out specifically this scrupulousness [blessing over a tiny portion of bread] over all other meticulous observances of mitzvos?
וְנִרְאֶה עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
It appears to follow what they said
(חֲגִיגָה י"ד.):
(Chagigah 14a):
נְשׂוּא פָנִים לְמַעְלָה כְּגוֹן רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא, נְשׂוּא פָנִים לְמַטָּה כְּגוֹן רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ בֵּיהּ קֵיסָר
"One held in favor on high, such as Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa; one held in favor below, such as Rabbi Abahu in the court of Caesar"
וּפֵירְשׁוּ בְּתוֹסָפוֹת שֶׁהָיָה בַּעַל מַעֲשִׂים דְּנָפִישׁ זְכוּתֵיהּ.
where Tosafos explained that he was a man of great deeds whose merit was abundant.
וְעִיקַּר הָעִנְיָן עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
And the core principle follows what they said
(בְּרָכוֹת י"ז:):
(Berachos 17b):
אָמַר רַב: בְּכָל יוֹם בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת מֵהַר חוֹרֵב: כָּל הָעוֹלָם נִיזּוֹן בִּשְׁבִיל חֲנִינָא בְּנִי, וַחֲנִינָא בְּנִי דַּי לוֹ בְּקַב חֲרוּבִים מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת.

"Rav said: Every day a heavenly voice goes forth from Mount Horeb declaring, 'The entire world is sustained for the sake of My son Chanina, while My son Chanina suffices with a kav of carobs from Friday evening to Friday evening.'"

הִנֵּה מֵימְרָא זוֹ דְּרַב הָיָה בִּזְמַן מְאוּחָר הַרְבֵּה מִימֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא, שֶׁהָיָה בִּזְמַן רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי, וְהֵיאַךְ יוֹצֵא הַקּוֹל בְּכָל יוֹם שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם נִיזּוֹן בִּשְׁבִיל חֲנִינָא

Now this statement of Rav was made in a much later era than the lifetime of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa (who lived in the time of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai), so how does the voice go forth every day proclaiming that the whole world is sustained for the sake of Chanina
(וְעַיֵּין בְּרַשִׁ"י חוּלִּין פ"ו. דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל חֲנִינָא)?
(see Rashi, Chullin 86a, s.v. Chanina)?
וְגַם מָה זֶה שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם גְּמַר אוֹמֵר בָּזֶה שֶׁחֲנִינָא בְּנִי דַּי לוֹ בְּקַב חֲרוּבִין?!
And also why does the voice always conclude with "while My son Chanina suffices with a kav of carobs"?!

אַךְ הָעִנְיָן הוּא שֶׁהַשֵּׁם "חֲנִינָא" הוּא מוּשְׁאָל לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר הוּא שָׁפֵל בְּעֵינָיו וְהוּא נוֹהֵג בְּמִדַּת הִסְתַּפְּקוּת, וּמַכִּיר שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁמַּמְצִיאִין לוֹ מְזוֹנֵי מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם—אֲפִילּוּ הַקַּב חֲרוּבִין—הוּא רַק מִצַּד "חֲנִינָא", מַה שֶּׁנֶּחֱנַן מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם, כִּי גַּם לָזֶה אֵינוֹ כְּדַאי מִצִּדּוֹ

However, the explanation is that the name Chanina (from chinam / chaninah, unearned grace) is an appellation borrowed for any soul who is lowly in his own eyes, practices contentment with little, and recognizes that whatever sustenance is provided to him from heaven—even a mere kav of carobs—comes purely out of chaninah (unmerited Divine grace), for even that he does not deserve on his own
כְּמוֹ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא בְּיָמָיו שֶׁהָיָה כֵּן בְּעֶצֶם נַפְשׁוֹ, וְלֹא נָשָׂא לִבּוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל מְזוֹנוֹת מְרוּוָּחִים כְּדֵי לְהָפִיס דַּעַת אִשְׁתּוֹ
just like Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa in his day, who embodied this in the very essence of his soul and could not bring himself to pray for abundant sustenance even to appease his wife
(תַּעֲנִית כ"ה.)
(Taanis 25a)
וּבְכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר יֵשׁ נְפָשׁוֹת כָּאֵלֶּה שֶׁבִּשְׁבִילָם ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹשֵׂא פָּנִים לְכָל הָעוֹלָם לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ מָזוֹן לְכָל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו דֵּי מַחְסוֹרָם.

and in every single generation there exist such souls for whose sake Hashem, may He be blessed, shows favor to the entire world by bestowing sustenance upon all His creatures sufficient for their needs.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁהֵם מְדַקְדְּקִים עַל עַצְמָם לְבָרֵךְ עַד כְּזַיִת וְעַד כְּבֵיצָה:
And this is what they meant by saying that Israel are scrupulous with themselves to recite blessings even over an olive's bulk or an egg's bulk:

וְלֹא בְּדִיבּוּר בִּלְבַד, רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ הוּא נוֹתֵן הוֹדָיָה וְשֶׁבַח לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּמְבָרֵךְ עַל מְזוֹנֵי שֶׁהִמְצִיא לוֹ, אֲפִילּוּ הַכְּזַיִת וְהַכְּבֵיצָה, הוּא רַק מִצַּד חֲנִינָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.

not with lip service alone, rather in absolute sincerity a person gives thanksgiving and praise to the Holy One, blessed is He, and blesses Him over the sustenance He has provided—recognizing that even an olive's bulk or an egg's bulk comes solely from His unearned grace, blessed be His Name.

וּמְזוֹנֵי דְּמִסְכְּנֵי כָּזֶה הוּא דּוֹמֶה בְּעֶצֶם כַּאֲכִילַת לֶחֶם מַצָּה שֶׁהוּא לֶחֶם עֹנִי וּמַאֲכַל שְׁבוּיִים, וְאָנוּ מִסְתַּפְּקִים בְּנַפְשֵׁנוּ בַּאֲכִילַת לֶחֶם זֶה כָּל יְמֵי הֶחָג וְנוֹתְנִין שֶׁבַח וְהוֹדָיָה לִשְׁמוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל הֶחָג, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: מוֹעֲדִים לְשִׂמְחָה,

And such sustenance of the poor is in its very essence identical to eating matzah, which is "bread of poverty" and the food of captives, yet we content ourselves in our souls with eating this bread throughout all the days of the festival while offering praise and thanksgiving to His Name, may He be blessed, all festival long, as we say "Appointed times for joy"
וּבִשְׁבִיל זֶה זוֹכִין לְהַשְׁפָּעַת בְּרָכָה וּמְזוֹנֵי לְכָל הַשָּׁנָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
and on account of this we merit the flow of blessing and sustenance for the entire year, as they said
(רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ט"ז.):
(Rosh Hashanah 16a):
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַפֶּסַח זְמַן תְּבוּאָה וְכוּלֵּי, כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתְבָּרֵךְ לָכֶם תְּבוּאָה שֶׁבַּשָּׂדוֹת.
"Because Pesach is the season of grain, etc., [bring the Omer] so that the grain in the fields may be blessed for you."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 61b — "All the sustenance of the world's inhabitants comes from above. The food that comes from heaven and earth is the food of the whole world — a coarse, thick food. The food that comes from higher up is a finer food, coming from the place where Judgment is found; and that is the food Israel ate when they went out of Egypt [matzah]."

A food higher than it, which is finer, comes from the place where Judgment rests, called Tzedek — and that is the food of the poor." It continues to the food higher still, the sustenance of the sick: "Hashem will sustain him upon the sickbed."

paragraphs.text: Berachos 20b — "The ministering angels said: Master of the world, Your Torah says, 'Who shows no favor,' yet You show favor to Israel — 'May Hashem lift His countenance to you'! He said: Shall I not show favor to Israel? I wrote, 'You shall eat and be satisfied and bless,' and they are scrupulous down to an olive's bulk and an egg's bulk." Rashi: an olive per Rabbi Meir, an egg per Rabbi Yehudah.

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 14a — "'And the one held in favor' (Yeshayahu 3:3) — one for whose sake favor is shown to his generation: above, such as Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa; below, such as Rabbi Abahu in the house of Caesar." Rashi: all are fed in his merit, as it says, "The whole world is sustained only for the sake of Chanina My son." Tosafos: for he was a man of deeds more than all his generation.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tiferes Yosef, Likkutei Shas, Taanis — “‘Every day a heavenly voice goes forth and says: The entire world is sustained for the sake of My son Chanina, and for My son Chanina a kav of carobs suffices.’ The matter is that Hashem gives a person only what is needed for the root of his soul; even what seems excess is needed for the root of his life. And so it was with Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, for whom a kav of carobs sufficed: because nothing more was needed for the root of his life except what was lacking to all Israel, and therefore the whole world was sustained for his sake.” Connection: Both read the heavenly voice as describing a soul whose own need is minimal and whose sustenance carries the world; Tiferes Yosef grounds it in each soul receiving only what its root requires.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yosef Chaim of Baghdad, Ben Yehoyada, Taanis 24b — “One may ask: why was it necessary to add that Chanina suffices with a kav of carobs? The early authorities explained ‘for the sake of (bishvil) Chanina’ as through his path (shevil) and channel. Often there are many accusers against the generation, and when the Holy One, blessed be He, gives an abundance of sustenance, they would hold it back from reaching those below because of our sins. So when Hashem wishes to hide the abundance from the accusers, He lowers it through the path of R. Chanina ben Dosa. They do not accuse when they see the abundance descending through his path because R. Chanina was content with the very least, a kav of carobs from Shabbos eve to Shabbos eve; since he takes no benefit from it, they pay no attention to it.” Connection: Ben Yehoyada answers the same question Rav Tzadok raises, why the voice ends with the kav of carobs: the world’s sustenance passes through the one who is content with little.

p: וּלְהָבִין הַלָּשׁוֹן: בְּכָל יוֹם בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת מֵהַר חוֹרֵב—מָה עִנְיַן הַר חוֹרֵב לְשֶׁפַע מָזוֹן?
Now, to understand the phrasing "Every day a heavenly voice goes forth from Mount Horeb"—what connection does Mount Horeb [Sinai] have to the flow of sustenance?
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ
One can explain this along the lines of what they said
(מוֹעֵד קָטָן כ"ח.):
(Moed Katan 28a):
בְּנֵי, חַיֵּי, וּמְזוֹנָא לָאו בִּזְכוּתָא תַּלְיָא אֶלָּא בְּמַזָּלָא.
"Children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit, rather on supernal flow (mazala)."
וְהִקְשׁוּ בְּתוֹסָפוֹת: הָא אֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל!
And Tosafos asked: Surely "Israel are not subject to planetary influence (mazal)"!
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
However, the explanation is as stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' ע"ט:)
שֶׁבְּחִינַת "אַיִן" הוּא הַמַּזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ דְּעַתִּיקָא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגָה, דְּקוֹצוֹ שֶׁל יוּ"ד דִּלְעֵילָּא רְמִיזָא לְ"אַיִן", וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר
that the aspect of Ayin ("Nothingness") is the mazal for Israel, which is the root of Atika above all human comprehension, for the upper tip of the Yud alludes to Ayin, and regarding this it is said
(שְׁמוּאֵל א' א', י'):
(I Shmuel 1:10):
וַתִּתְפַּלֵּל חַנָּה עַל הֲוָיָ"ה
"And Channah prayed upon (al) Hashem"
דַּיְיקָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
specifically al ("above" Havayah), as brought in the holy Zohar
(ibid. 65b),
וְאִיהוּ לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אָדָם, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
and it is above human grasp, just as they said
(מְגִילָּה ג'.):
(Megillah 3a):
אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא חָזוּ, מַזְלַיְיהוּ חָזוּ
"Even though they themselves do not see, their mazal sees"
וּמִשָּׁם בָּא הַשֶּׁפַע מְזוֹנָא.
and from there comes the flow of sustenance.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ
And this is what they said
(פְּסָחִים קי"ח.)
(Pesachim 118a)
שֶׁנִּקְרָא הַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וּמְחַלֵּק מָזוֹן לְכָל בְּרִיּוֹתָיו, וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשְׁבַּ"ם שֶׁדָּבָר גָּדוֹל הוּא

that Psalm 136 is called the Great Hallel because the Holy One, blessed is He, sits in the heights of the universe and distributes food to all His creatures, and the Rashbam explained "because it is a great thing"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁ"גָּדוֹל" מוֹרֶה עַל תַּכְלִית הַגַּדְלוּת שֶׁאֵין לְמַעְלָה הֵימֶנּוּ, וְהוּא בְּחִינַת עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
meaning that "Great" denotes the ultimate greatness beyond which there is nothing higher, which is the aspect of Atika Kadisha, and as it is said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"א, ח'):
(Bereishis 21:8):
וַיַּעַשׂ אַבְרָהָם מִשְׁתֶּה גָדוֹל,
"And Avraham made a great feast,"
וְאִיתָא
and it is stated
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה נ"ג, י'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 53:10):
גְּדוֹל הָעוֹלָמִים הָיָה שָׁם
"The Great One of the worlds was there"
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן לְרֶמֶז הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, שֶׁמִּילַת יִצְחָק שֶׁהָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה, וְזֶה מוֹרֶה שֶׁהוּא מְקוּשָּׁר בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַקְּדוּשָּׁה לְמַעְלָה מִן הַדַּעַת.

which also alludes to the same point, regarding the circumcision of Yitzchak, who was the first to be circumcised at eight days old, signifying that he is bound to the root of holiness above conscious intellect (Da'as).
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ
And concerning this they said
(גְּמָרָא שָׁם):
(Gemara, ibid.):
קָשִׁין מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם כִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
"A person's sustenance is as difficult [miraculous] as the Splitting of the Sea, as it is said
(תְּהִלִּים קל"ו, י"ג):
(Tehillim 136:13):
לְגֹזֵר יַם סוּף לִגְזָרִים,
'To Him Who divided the Sea of Reeds into parts,'
וְסָמוּךְ לֵיהּ
and juxtaposed to it is
(פָּסוּק כ"ה):
(verse 25):
נֹתֵן לֶחֶם לְכָל בָּשָׂר
'Who gives bread to all flesh'"
וְהִקְשָׁה בְּמַהַרְשָׁ"א: הָא יֵשׁ בֵּין הַסְּמִיכוּת כַּמָּה עִנְיָנִים אֲחֵרִים בַּקְּרָא!
and the Maharsha asked: Surely between those two verses there are several other topics in the psalm!
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן: כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ, דְּעִנְיַן קְרִיעַת יַם סוּף הָיָה גַּם כֵּן לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגָה, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה הַקִּטְרוּג: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנּוּ אֵלּוּ מֵאֵלּוּ
However, the explanation is as we said: the Splitting of the Sea also occurred from a realm beyond human comprehension, for in truth there was the prosecution "How are these different from those?"
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ז'),
(Shemos Rabbah 21:7),
אַךְ אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
yet it is stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' מ"ח.):
מַה תִּצְעַק אֵלַי? בְּעַתִּיקָא תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא
"'Why do you cry out to Me (eilai)?'—the matter depends upon Atika"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁנִּתְבָּרְרוּ אָז יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם קְשׁוּרִים בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ עֶלְיוֹן לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגָה.
meaning Israel were clarified then as being bound to the Supernal Root above all comprehension.
וְזֶהוּ מַמָּשׁ עִנְיַן הַמְּזוֹנוֹת שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת אֱנוֹשִׁי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
And this is the exact nature of sustenance, which likewise operates beyond human comprehension, as they said
(מוֹעֵד קָטָן שָׁם):
(Moed Katan, ibid.):
רַבָּה וְרַב חִסְדָּא תַּרְוַיְיהוּ צַדִּיקֵי גְּמוּרֵי נִינְהוּ, מָר מְצַלֵּי וְכוּלֵּי; בֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא וְכוּלֵּי וּבֵיהּ רַבָּה וְכוּלֵּי

"Rabbah and Rav Chisda were both completely righteous men; one prayed [for rain and it came], etc.; yet the house of Rav Chisda [had abundance], whereas the house of Rabbah [lacked even barley bread]"

וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן "קָשִׁין מְזוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם", דְּהוּא קוּשְׁיָא דְּמַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה זֶה מִזֶּה, וְהוּא כִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן הַקּוּשְׁיָא: מַה נִּשְׁתַּנּוּ אֵלּוּ מֵאֵלּוּ, רַק בְּמַזָּלָא תַּלְיָא שֶׁהוּא הָ"אַיִן" שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגָה.

and this is the meaning of "a person's sustenance is kashin [a difficult question]": it poses the question of "Why does this person differ from that person?", just like the Splitting of the Sea which posed the question "How are these different from those?"—both depend solely on mazala, which is Ayin above all grasp.
וְעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ גַּם כֵּן בַּגְּמָרָא
And to this they also alluded in the Gemara
(פְּסָחִים שָׁם):
(Pesachim, ibid.):

עֶשְׂרִים וְשִׁשָּׁה "כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ" שֶׁבְּהַלֵּל הַגָּדוֹל נֶגֶד עֶשְׂרִים וְשִׁשָּׁה דּוֹרוֹת שֶׁמִּבְּרִיאַת הָעוֹלָם עַד מַתַּן תּוֹרָה שֶׁזָּן אוֹתָם בְּחַסְדּוֹ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ

that the twenty-six refrains of "for His kindness is forever" in the Great Hallel correspond to the twenty-six generations from Creation until the Giving of the Torah, whom God sustained purely through His kindness because they did not yet have attachment to the Supernal Root
דְּעִיקַּר הִתְקַשְּׁרוּת הוּא עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
for the primary attachment to the Root comes through the power of the Torah, as it is said
(אִיּוֹב כ"ח, י"ב):
וְהַחָכְמָה מֵאַיִן תִּמָּצֵא
"And wisdom, from where (me'ayin) shall it be found?"
דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
for it is stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' קכ"א.):
וְהַחָכְמָה נָפְקַת מֵאֲתַר דְּאִיקְרֵי קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת "אַיִן", בְּחִינַת עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא,
"And wisdom emerges from the place called the Holy of Holies," which is the aspect of Ayin, Atika Kadisha,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
and along the lines of what they said
(סוֹטָה כ"א.):
(Sotah 21a):
בְּמִי שֶׁמֵּשִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּ"אַיִן",
"In one who renders himself like nothing (ayin),"

וְאֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִתְקַיֶּימֶת אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁמֵּמִית עַצְמוֹ עָלֶיהָ, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהוּא בְּתַכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת בְּעַצְמוֹ וְיֵשׁ לוֹ מִדַּת הִסְתַּפְּקוּת, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה טַל תּוֹרָה מְחַיֵּיהוּ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת טַלָּא דְּנָטִיף מֵעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא

and "words of Torah endure only in one who kills himself over them," meaning one who is in utmost lowliness in his own eyes and practices contentment, through which the dew of Torah revives him, which is the dew dripping from Atika Kadisha
וְעַל יְדֵי נְפָשׁוֹת כָּאֵלּוּ נִשְׁפָּע שֶׁפַע מָזוֹן לְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם, שֶׁהֵם מַמְשִׁיכִים הַשֶּׁפַע מִמָּקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ, בְּחִינַת "אַיִן", מַזָּלָא.
and through such souls the flow of sustenance is bestowed upon all inhabitants of the world, for they draw down abundance from the lofty place of Ayin, Mazala.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: בְּכָל יוֹם בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת מֵהַר חוֹרֵב—הַיְינוּ כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה—שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם נִיזּוֹן בִּשְׁבִיל חֲנִינָא בְּנִי, הַיְינוּ בִּשְׁבִיל מִי שֶׁמֵּשִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּ"אַיִן", וְהַכֹּל אֶצְלוֹ מִצַּד חֲנִינָא מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְזֶהוּ: וַחֲנִינָא בְּנִי דַּי לוֹ בְּקַב חֲרוּבִין כָּאָמוּר.

And this is what they said: "Every day a heavenly voice goes forth from Mount Horeb"—meaning the power of the Torah—proclaiming "The entire world is sustained for the sake of My son Chanina," that is, for the sake of anyone who makes himself like Ayin and views everything he receives as unearned grace (chaninah) from Hashem, may He be blessed, which is "while My son Chanina suffices with a kav of carobs," as stated.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Divrei Soferim 30 — “They said, ‘The entire world is sustained for the sake of Chanina,’ even though there were many great righteous men in that generation; but they all had plenty at the time of sustenance, and Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa alone was very poor, and his sustenance was as difficult as the Splitting of the Sea, which depends on Atika, for a new gate had to be opened for him in the drawing of something from nothing, which is the mazal for Israel. Through the drawing of sustenance to him the flow of sustenance opened for the whole world; only, a kav sufficed him.” Connection: The same chain from Chanina’s poverty through ‘as difficult as the Splitting of the Sea’ to Atika and mazala; it adds that the world is fed through his own need, which opens the gate for everyone.
